title: Data Airlock: configurable export & external-sharing lock with network allowlist
creator: Aisha Kumar
description:
Background: Enterprise customers require an 'airlock' that prevents data leaving the org boundary and disables share/export UX while preserving developer workflows. This ticket implements a boolean 'Data Airlock' admin toggle plus granular sub-controls: network allowlist (IP/CIDR), external-sharing disable, and export-permissions scoped by role. It must integrate with RBAC v2 so that the toggle respects role overrides, surface audit events for all state transitions, and tie into SSO/SAML group mappings for admins.
Goals: 1) Add org-scoped toggle and per-team overrides. 2) Implement persistent network allowlist enforced at API-gateway and Console UI. 3) Block or redact public-sharing links and disable 'export' buttons for enrolled orgs. 4) Emit structured audit logs compatible with our SIEM.
Constraints: Must not degrade runtime latency, must be backward-compatible with orgs using legacy admin flags, and support private deployments with local KMS.
acceptance_criteria: Admin Control in Console: Org admins can enable 'Data Airlock' with a single toggle and configure an IP/CIDR allowlist in the same flow.
RBAC v2 integration: Role-based exceptions are supported (e.g., 'Security Compliance' role can be granted temporary export rights).
API enforcement: All export endpoints return 403 for blocked orgs and log an audit event with reason and actor.
Sharing UI: Public share link creation is disabled in Console and SDKs for locked orgs; attempts produce contextual UX explaining the policy.
Audit logging: All toggle flips, allowlist changes, and blocked export/share attempts create structured audit entries (JSON) with actor, timestamp, target, policy_id.
SSO mapping: when SAML/SSO is enabled, groups mapped to admin roles can toggle and see airlock configuration.
E2E tests: automated tests cover policy enforcement at gateway layer and browser UI tests for share/export buttons.
work_log: 2026-02-28: Ticket opened by Aisha; initial scoping and risk assessment completed.
2026-03-02: Spike: prototyped allowlist enforcement at edge via Envoy RBAC config. Results: feasible with no measurable p99 latency increase (PRF-618).
2026-03-04: Decision: implement Console UI as 'Airlock' with nested controls (Allowlist, Sharing, Exports). Chosen to reuse existing org-settings components to minimize UI churn.
2026-03-06: Backend schema change proposed: add org_policy table row 'data_airlock' with JSON blob. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/14567 (draft).
2026-03-09: Security review kickoff scheduled. Noted need to include audit event schema v2 to align with SIEM ingestion.
2026-03-12: Implemented gateway enforcement for export endpoints and added unit tests. Backend PR link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/14589
review_feedback: PM (Jordan Park): prefer 'Airlock' naming for customer clarity; asked UX copy for blocked actions to include recommended remediation steps.
Design (Lena Ortiz): suggested inline explainers in Console and break the allowlist into 'management' vs 'service' subnets.
Security (Dr. Emil Novak): require HSM key reference for audit log signing in Private deployments — added to follow-up.
Eng Lead (Marcus Li): requested explicit performance benchmarks before GA; added benchmark suite to definition of done.
notes: Customer ask: large financial customer requested export lock with SSO-enforced admin audit — sales ticket 4512-FT

Edge enforcement approach considered alternatives: token-scoped checks (higher app load) vs. Envoy RBAC (single point of policy). Chosen: hybrid — Envoy denies outbound export API calls, app returns 403 with explanation for telemetry.
